scope: Closed Japan/China campaign; convoy raiding, interdiction and Kido Butai remain disabled.

rules.clarification: RCL-017 adopted, revised: a patrol plane that lets ships pass takes no part in their battles in its zone and does not stop their amphibious assaults, but they may attack it anew and it then chooses again (RB 0.3); once it has fought and survived, it stops their amphibious assault. RCL-020 adopted: attacked by ships already in its zone, it chooses by the patrol rule before any scramble, and staying out costs it nothing
RCL-020 adopted: a patrol plane attacked in its sea zone chooses before ships scramble; if it stays out and nothing else of its side defends, there is no battle to scramble into
RCL-018 adopted: an assault whose sea zone is not cleared, or whose transports all retreat, is called off as Combat ends; its cargo stays aboard

rules.reason: Both dotted crossings can be bypassed without another sea-zone move; ordinary sea-zone entry is not automatically a crossing. See geography_review.

adopted_clarifications.ruling: The fleet evacuating the damaged port defends; the enemy fleet already at sea attacks, including combat during a third nation calendar turn.
adopted_clarifications.authority: The Warden developer clarification in a user-provided Discord screenshot, 2026-10-23; supersedes the provisional user ruling.
adopted_clarifications.authority_detail: The developer example is Commonwealth evacuation into Italian ships during German bombing. Applying these roles to KMT evacuation into CCP ships during Japan's turn extends the same principle to three alliances; that exact example was not in the message.

adopted_clarifications.ruling: A patrol plane that lets ships pass shares its sea zone with them (RB 0.3): it takes no part in their screening battle or the battle where their route ends, and it does not count against their screening or amphibious assault. The ships may still attack it in Combat Movement, a new combat move; it then chooses again by the patrol rule (RCL-020), before any scramble. If it fights, it no longer counts as having declined combat, and if it survives it stops their amphibious assault.
adopted_clarifications.authority: User ruling in chat, 2026-11-04: "RCL 017 is wrong, it can accept later after it passed", reversing the same day's ruling that a refusal settles combat with those ships for the turn.
adopted_clarifications.authority_detail: RB 0.3 lists a declined Maritime Air Patrol among the cases where units at war share a sea zone, which lasts until one power makes a new combat move against the other units there. RB 9.4.2 and 10.8.1 exempt an aircraft on MAP which declined combat from screening and from the amphibious assault's clearing.

adopted_clarifications.ruling: An amphibious assault whose sea zone still holds Enemy surface ships or aircraft after its naval combat, for example ships scrambled into it, is called off, and its land units stay aboard their transports for the rest of the turn. A transport that retreats takes its cargo out of the assault, which goes ahead with any cargo still in the cleared sea zone.
adopted_clarifications.authority: User ruling in chat, 2026-11-03: "Yes, adopt it", to the proposal that an assault from an uncleared sea is called off with the infantry staying aboard.
adopted_clarifications.authority_detail: RB 10.8.1 requires those units to be eliminated first and lets defenders scramble, but does not say what happens when they survive. Found as a self-play dead end on the night of 2 November 2026 (seed 4238465544019468396), where the engine could neither start nor drop the assault.

adopted_clarifications.ruling: A patrol plane attacked by ships already in its sea zone chooses whether to fight by the patrol rule, not the carrier rule: it may stay out unless the Attacker has aircraft with an attack value present, and staying out costs it nothing. It chooses before any scramble, so if it stays out and no other unit of its side defends there is no battle and nothing to scramble into. A plane that stays out has declined combat again and does not count against those ships' screening or amphibious assault.
adopted_clarifications.authority: User ruling in chat, 2026-11-04: "of course we need to fix the MAP and the aircraft on a carrier difference, they are not the same", with the order "the MAP plane can choose to fight again, or not. Only then the ships can scramble into this [sea zone] because this is combat phase."
adopted_clarifications.authority_detail: RB 9.3.1 and 9.4 give the patrol plane's choice only for ships entering its zone; RB 10.7 step 2 gives aircraft on carriers a choice after scrambles, and a carrier aircraft kept on deck is lost with the battle. The engine had applied the carrier rule to patrol planes since its first version. Found while checking RCL-017 on 4 November 2026.
